ct_tree_tops_bethel_ct.blurb: Tree Tops is a compact bouldering area in Bethel, Connecticut, made up of schist blocks sitting beneath a small cliff. A large block at the foot of the cliff is the main landmark, and further down the slope two clusters of boulders hold most of the lines. About 19 problems are described, running from VB-level warm-ups through the middle grades and up to a handful of V7s, so there is something for a mixed group. Landings are reported as fine at the upper blocks and mostly good lower down. Expect poison ivy around the boulders and plenty of bugs in spring.

ct_samp_mortar.blurb: Samp Mortar is a bouldering spot on schist in Fairfield, Connecticut, set in a small town park and sharing a broken cliff band with the neighbouring Mt. Laurel boulders. The walk in passes the remains of an old quartz quarry before dropping into a glen of big blocks. Roughly 19 problems range from easy slabs and warm-ups at the low end, through a solid block of V1 to V7 lines, to a single very hard test piece. The problems vary from one-move wonders to tall highballs, so check landings before committing on the big ones.

de_main_roped_climbing_wall.blurb: This is the main wall at Alapocas Run State Park, just outside Wilmington, Delaware, on gneiss. Climbing here is mostly top-rope, with about fifteen routes from easy slabs in the 5.2 range up to the low 5.11s, plus a few boulder problems and a single trad line. The left side of the wall is noticeably shorter, while the centre and right carry most of the climbs. The wall catches sun through much of the day in high season, and the park around it is a wooded setting above the Brandywine River.

wa_sehome_arboretum_climbs.blurb: Sehome Arboretum is a wooded hilltop beside the Western Washington University campus in Bellingham, with scattered sandstone boulders and small cliff bands. Most of the climbing here is bouldering, from the easiest grades up to about V6, with one sport line around 5.9 and a top-rope around 5.10. Roped routes are short, so some feel close to boulder problems, and landings can be poor, so pads and spotters matter. The sandstone turns fragile when wet and can take many dry days to recover in winter. Paths through the woods see steady foot traffic.

_skipped.wa_spire_rock_climbs: SPIRE Rock is a man-made artificial climbing structure, not a natural crag
